corrections.report_value: Efforts to standardize agent interactions have led to protocols like Anthropic's Model-Compute Protocol (MCP) for model-tool invocation and Google's Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol for inter-agent communication. While these protocols facilitate connectivity and message passing, they primarily operate at the level of invocation, leaving the internal states of agents and their resources opaque. They generally do not provide mechanisms for lifecycle management, version tracking, or controlled mutation of internal components, which are prerequisites for systematic self-evolution.
corrections.authoritative_excerpt: Although protocols such as MCP~\cite{anthropic2025agentskills} and A2A~\cite{google2025a2a} have standardized connectivity for model-tool invocation and inter-agent communication, they operate solely at the level of invocation and message passing, leaving internal resource states opaque. Neither provides mechanisms for lifecycle management, version lineage, or controlled state mutation, which are precisely the requirements of a closed-loop evolutionary system. Bridging this gap calls for a dedicated protocol addressing three essential properties: \textbf{Decoupling}, so that resources such as prompts, tools, and memory are managed as independent entities rather than tightly coupled code; \textbf{Safety \& Auditability}, through strict version control and rollback to ensure every evolutionary step is traceable and reversible; and \textbf{Formalism}, via standardized operators (e.g., reflect, propose, verify) that convert heuristic modifications into a rigorous control loop.
corrections.replacement_interpretation: The retained source uses MCP without expanding it; the raw report’s “Model-Compute Protocol” expansion is unsupported and rejected.
